b: Two classical games in a single day

Following Tuesday's blitz tournament, the main event of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot began in Budapest on Wednesday. The 24 participants were divided into four groups of six, playing a double round-robin at the innovative (for elite tournaments) "fast classic" time control of 45 minutes plus 30-second increments per move.

Notably, this is the first time FIDE has applied such a time control to an elite tournament with games counting towards the official classical ratings. With two rounds scheduled each day, some of the strongest players in the world are playing two rated classical games on the same day (a rare if not unheard of occurrence in the history of the game). On Wednesday, each participant faced the same opponent twice, once with each colour.

Another distinctive feature is the use of football-style scoring: 3 points for a win, 1 for a draw and none for a loss. The effect was already apparent in Group C, where Magnus Carlsen and Anish Giri drew both their games to finish on 2 points each, behind Ian Nepomniachtchi, who collected a win and a draw for 4 points, and also behind Shakhriyar Mamedyarov and Haik Martirosyan, who exchanged victories with the black pieces to score 3 points each. Under this scoring system, a win and a loss are worth more than two draws.

No player managed to start the group stage with back-to-back wins on Wednesday. The top six scorers finished the day with 4 points out of a possible 6: Jan-Krzysztof Duda and Alireza Firouzja in Group A, Fabiano Caruana and Le Quang Liem in Group B, Ian Nepomniachtchi in Group C and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave in Group D.
